newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines says no more rice imports this year.
newsitem.headline: Philippines says no more rice imports this year.

text.p: The Philippines will not import any more rice this year, the state National Food Authority said on Sunday.

A National Food Authority statement said NFA administrator Joemari Gerochi had told local grains producers that the government was no longer buying rice from abroad in face of an expected bumper hearvest this season.
It said the NFA had allocated 3.5 billion pesos from now until December to buy a targetted quantity of 8.8 million bags of palay (unmilled rice).

A Department of Agriculture official said in August the Philippines was unlikely to need further rice imports for the rest of the year because it had a buffer stock of 1.4 million tonnes of rice, the staple food of the country's 68 million people.
A rice shortage last year sent prices soaring and caused a sharp rise in inflation to double digits.
The Philippines imported 846,000 tonnes in the year to August, the latest figures available.
